title: Singleton decomposition of a finite measure
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite measurable space (finite and discrete)
μ is a finite measure on Ω
S is an arbitrary subset of Ω
replaced:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space, $\mu$ a finite measure on it, and $S
\subseteq \Omega$ any set.  Then
\[
  \mu^{\mathbb{R}}(S) \;=\; \sum_{\omega \in \Omega}
    \begin{cases} \mu^{\mathbb{R}}(\{\omega\}) & \text{if } \omega \in S, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
\]
In other words, a finite measure on a finite measurable space is determined by and
recovers as a finite sum over its singleton masses.
